name: North American Parts Center Kentucky - Hebron KY

fieldNotes.truckGate: Large fenced Toyota parts-distribution hub set back from the public road (Aero Pkwy); a controlled access road funnels traffic onto the property. Truck access is gated.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Set true on the strong prior that NAPCK — a critical national Toyota parts hub feeding 12 US PDCs — runs a staffed truck-gate checkpoint. A standalone booth could not be positively isolated in imagery (truck-side access is tree-screened from the public road); flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False on the same logic — but the guard-shack vs. remote-check-in split is genuinely uncertain here; flagged for human review.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Very large DC — dozens of dock doors with trailers backed in along the SW long face and the SE face; band 50+. Exact count obscured by trailers/canopies — estimate flagged.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer drop yards: a large cul-de-sac trailer-storage lot off the SW and additional rows along the SE; many dozens of parked trailers. Band 50+.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Docks appear on two distinct building faces (SW and SE) suggesting separate inbound/outbound dock clusters — set true at medium confidence, flagged.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide internal truck roads and a long approach drive give physical room to add an express/bypass lane at the gate.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur visible running into the property.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Industrial-park setting near the CVG airport / Hebron, KY — edge-of-town industrial amid open land and other big-box DCs; classified Rural per rubric. CVG corridor has good connectivity, so connectivityIssue = false.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box ~93 acres capturing the warehouse plus its surrounding drop yards and parking.

citations.claim: NAPCK is Toyota largest parts procurement/distribution facility under one roof; 86-acre Boone County KY site; ~540 team; ~500k parts/day

verification.rationale: Active Toyota parts procurement/distribution hub feeding 12 US PDCs; self-attested current operations.
